                // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored

            }
        } finally {
            // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
            src.delete();
            // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored

        } finally {
            // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
            src.delete();
        }
    }

FILE: app/src/androidTest/java/com/example/hello/BackgroundConversionResilienceTest.java

package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertNotNull;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertNull;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import android.content.Context;
import android.content.Intent;

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4;
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry;

import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;

import java.io.File;
import java.io.RandomAccessFile;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Regression coverage for the reported "background converter completely
 * stops" behaviour. The old worker parked forever while a take was open for
 * editing (or while any reader held its raw); editing the same take and
 * previewing its raw must now both leave the conversion running to
 * completion in the background.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class BackgroundConversionResilienceTest {

    private Context ctx() {
        return InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().getTargetContext();
    }

    private File makeRaw(Context ctx, String name) throws Exception {
        File takes = RecordingEngine.takesDir(ctx);
        File f = new File(takes, name + "_" + System.nanoTime() + ".wav");
        int frames = 48000 * 2;
        RandomAccessFile w = new RandomAccessFile(f, "rw");
        try {
            w.setLength(0);
            w.write(Dsp.wavFloatHeader(2, 48000, (long) frames * 2 * 4));
            float[] buf = new float[frames * 2];
            for (int i = 0; i < frames * 2; i++) {
                buf[i] = (float) Math.sin(i * 0.05) * 0.4f;
            }
            Dsp.writeFloatsLE(w, buf, 0, buf.length);
        } finally {
            w.close();
        }
        return f;
    }

    private void launchActivity() {
        android.app.Instrumentation instr =
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation();
        Intent i = new Intent(instr.getTargetContext(), MainActivity.class);
        i.addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK
                | Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK);
        instr.startActivitySync(i);
    }

    @Test
    public void conversionFinishesWhileTheSameTakeIsOpenForEditing()
            throws Exception {
        launchActivity();
        Context ctx = ctx();
        RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
        engine.abortAndDelete();
        File raw = makeRaw(ctx, "Background edit");
        ConversionJob job = null;
        Take finished = null;
        try {
            job = ConversionJobs.enqueue(ctx, raw, "Background edit",
                    RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.M4A, 2000);
            assertNotNull("job was not enqueued", job);
            // Exactly the old park condition: an edit session for the same
            // synthetic take id, plus a live raw reader (preview/import).
            EditLink.save(ctx, job.takeId(), "Background edit",
                    raw.getAbsolutePath());
            engine.attachExisting(ctx, raw, "Background edit", 2,
                    RecordingEngine.payloadBytesOf(raw));
            ConversionJobs.beginRawRead(raw.getAbsolutePath());
            assertTrue("session should be open", engine.hasSession());
            assertTrue("raw should be marked as read",
                    ConversionJobs.rawIsBeingRead(raw.getAbsolutePath()));

            ConversionService.startJob(ctx, job.jobId);

            long deadline = System.currentTimeMillis() + 60_000L;
            while (ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId) != null
                    && System.currentTimeMillis() < deadline) {
                Thread.sleep(100);
            }
            assertNull("conversion stalled while the take was being edited",
                    ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId));

            List<Take> takes = TakesRepository.all();
            for (Take t : takes) {
                if ("Background edit".equals(t.title)) finished = t;
            }
            assertNotNull("finished take not in library", finished);
            assertTrue("finished file missing", finished.hasFile());
            assertTrue("reader must defer raw deletion until it closes",
                    raw.exists());
        } finally {
            ConversionJobs.endRawRead(raw.getAbsolutePath());
            engine.clearSession();
            EditLink.clear(ctx);
            if (job != null) ConversionJobs.cancel(job.jobId, true);
            if (finished != null) TakesRepository.delete(finished.id);
            if (finished != null) {
                // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
                new File(finished.filePath).delete();
            }
            // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
            raw.delete();
            // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
            new File(raw.getAbsolutePath() + ".pending").delete();
        }
    }
}

FILE: app/src/androidTest/java/com/example/hello/ConversionBenchTest.java

package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import android.content.Context;
import android.util.Log;

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4;
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry;

import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;

import java.io.File;
import java.io.RandomAccessFile;

/**
 * Throughput probe for the save path. Prints MB/s per conversion so the
 * effect of the bulk-conversion work is measurable rather than asserted.
 *
 * <p>Runs on whatever device/emulator it is pushed to; emulator numbers are
 * pessimistic, so treat them as a floor.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class ConversionBenchTest {

    private static final String TAG = "CONVBENCH";
    private static final double SECONDS = 20.0;
    private static final int SR = 48000;
    private static final int CH = 2;

    private File makeSource(String name) throws Exception {
        Context ctx = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
                .getTargetContext();
        File f = new File(ctx.getCacheDir(), name);
        int frames = (int) (SR * SECONDS);
        RandomAccessFile w = new RandomAccessFile(f, "rw");
        try {
            w.setLength(0);
            w.write(Dsp.wavFloatHeader(CH, SR, (long) frames * CH * 4));
            float[] buf = new float[8192 * CH];
            double phase = 0;
            for (int off = 0; off < frames; off += 8192) {
                int n = Math.min(8192, frames - off);
                for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                    // Mix of tones + noise so it is not trivially compressible.
                    float v = (float) (0.30 * Math.sin(phase)
                            + 0.15 * Math.sin(phase * 2.7)
                            + 0.05 * (Math.random() * 2 - 1));
                    buf[i * 2] = v;
                    buf[i * 2 + 1] = v * 0.9f;
                    phase += 2 * Math.PI * 220 / SR;
                }
                Dsp.writeFloatsLE(w, buf, 0, n * CH);
            }
        } finally {
            w.close();
        }
        return f;
    }

    private void bench(String label, File src, long rawBytes, Runner r)
            throws Exception {
        File out = new File(src.getParentFile(), "bench_" + label + ".tmp");
        // warm the page cache / JIT
        long t0 = System.nanoTime();
        r.run(src, out);
        long ms = (System.nanoTime() - t0) / 1_000_000L;
        double mb = rawBytes / 1048576d;
        double mbps = (mb / (ms / 1000d));
        Log.i(TAG, String.format(java.util.Locale.US,
                "%s: %d bytes in %d ms = %.1f MB/s (%.2fx realtime)", label,
                rawBytes, ms, mbps, SECONDS / (ms / 1000d)));
        long outBytes = out.exists() ? out.length() : 0L;
        // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
        out.delete();
        assertTrue(label + " produced no output (" + outBytes + " bytes)",
                outBytes > 0);
    }

    private interface Runner {
        void run(File src, File dst) throws Exception;
    }

    @Test
    public void conversionThroughput() throws Exception {
        File src = makeSource("bench_in.wav");
        long rawBytes = src.length();
        Log.i(TAG, String.format(java.util.Locale.US,
                "source: %.1f MB, %.0fs of 48k stereo",
                rawBytes / 1048576d, SECONDS));

        bench("wav16", src, rawBytes, (a, b) ->
                FormatConverter.toWav16(a, b, null));
        bench("wav24", src, rawBytes, (a, b) ->
                FormatConverter.toWav24(a, b, null));
        bench("m4a", src, rawBytes, (a, b) ->
                FormatConverter.toM4a(a, b, 256000, null));
        bench("flac", src, rawBytes, (a, b) ->
                FormatConverter.toFlac(a, b, null));

        // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
        src.delete();
    }
}

FILE: app/src/androidTest/java/com/example/hello/ConversionConcurrencyTest.java

package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertFalse;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertNotNull;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertSame;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import android.content.Context;

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4;
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry;

import org.junit.Rule;
import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;

import java.io.File;
import java.io.RandomAccessFile;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * The user-reported contention cases around the background converter.
 *
 * <p>Three regressions are covered: switching save format mid-recording must
 * not park the studio on a multi-second inline drain (the restarted encoder
 * has re-encoded one chunk but is still seconds behind), a save that gives up
 * on the fast path must leave no encoder thread writing the part file the
 * worker is about to claim, and a sweep must never delete a live capture's
 * partial output or re-arm a job that is already tracked.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class ConversionConcurrencyTest {

    @Rule
    public androidx.test.rule.GrantPermissionRule mic =
            androidx.test.rule.GrantPermissionRule.grant(
                    android.Manifest.permission.RECORD_AUDIO);

    private Context ctx() {
        return InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().getTargetContext();
    }

    private boolean streamThreadAlive() {
        for (Thread t : Thread.getAllStackTraces().keySet()) {
            if ("takeone-stream-enc".equals(t.getName()) && t.isAlive()) return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

    private RecordingEngine recordedSession(String name, SaveFormat fmt,
                                           long millis) throws Exception {
        RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
        engine.abortAndDelete();
        engine.startNewSession(ctx(), name, 2);
        engine.beginStreaming(ctx(), RecordPreset.MEMO, fmt);
        engine.startCapture(ctx(),
                android.media.MediaRecorder.AudioSource.MIC);
        Thread.sleep(millis);
        engine.pauseCapture();
        return engine;
    }

    /**
     * Changing the save format while recording restarts the incremental
     * encoder from the top of the raw file. It reports progress after its
     * first chunk, so a naive "has it started?" check sent the save into a
     * full-tail inline drain and froze the studio for seconds.
     */
    @Test
    public void formatSwitchSaveSkipsStallAndGoesBackground() throws Exception {
        RecordingEngine engine = recordedSession("Format switch", SaveFormat.M4A,
                12000);
        // The user changed the format on the last moment: same take, new
        // encoder from the start, whole recording unencoded again.
        assertTrue("expected a restarted encoder",
                engine.restartStreaming(ctx(), RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.OPUS));
        StreamingEncoder sess = engine.streaming();
        assertNotNull("restarted encoder must exist", sess);
        // Give the fresh pump just enough time to encode its first chunk: it
        // looks productive while being almost entirely behind.
        long untilEncoded = System.currentTimeMillis() + 4000;
        while (sess.framesEncoded() == 0
                && System.currentTimeMillis() < untilEncoded) {
            Thread.sleep(50);
        }
        assertTrue("encoder never reported progress", sess.framesEncoded() > 0);
        // The invariant below only exists while a real multi-second backlog is
        // left: a restarted encoder can finish a very short (near-silent) take
        // inside the poll interval above, and then inline adoption is the
        // correct, fast path rather than a stall.
        org.junit.Assume.assumeTrue("no multi-second backlog to exercise",
                sess.unencodedFrames() > 72000L);

        long t0 = System.currentTimeMillis();
        ConversionJobs.SaveResult r = ConversionJobs.dispatchSave(ctx(),
                RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.OPUS, null);
        long elapsed = System.currentTimeMillis() - t0;

        assertFalse("a take with a multi-second backlog cannot adopt inline",
                r.adopted);
        assertNotNull("save must hand off to the worker", r.job);
        assertTrue("save blocked the studio for " + elapsed + "ms",
                elapsed < 2000);
        ConversionJobs.cancel(r.job.jobId, false);
    }

    /**
     * Giving up on the fast path used to unlink the part file while the
     * encoder thread was still writing it, then hand the same path to the
     * worker: two writers, one container, corrupt output.
     */
    @Test
    public void abandonedAdoptLeavesNoEncoderOnThePartFile() throws Exception {
        RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
        engine.abortAndDelete();
        // A long take on disk, so the backlog is huge by construction and the
        // test does not depend on how fast the emulator happens to encode.
        File raw = new File(RecordingEngine.takesDir(ctx()),
                "abandon.wav");
        long frames = 48000L * 60L;
        writeRaw(raw, (int) frames);
        engine.attachExisting(ctx(), raw, "Abandoned adopt", 2,
                frames * 4L * 2L);
        engine.beginStreaming(ctx(), RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.M4A);
        StreamingEncoder sess = engine.streaming();
        assertNotNull("streaming encoder did not start", sess);
        File part = sess.partFile();

        // Let the fresh pump encode its first chunk: from here it looks
        // productive while being a minute behind, exactly the state that used
        // to send the save into a full inline drain.
        long untilEncoded = System.currentTimeMillis() + 8000;
        while (sess.framesEncoded() == 0
                && System.currentTimeMillis() < untilEncoded) {
            Thread.sleep(50);
        }
        assertTrue("encoder never reported progress", sess.framesEncoded() > 0);
        assertTrue("expected a large unencoded backlog",
                sess.unencodedFrames() > 48000L);

        ConversionJobs.SaveResult r = ConversionJobs.dispatchSave(ctx(),
                RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.M4A, null);
        assertFalse("a minute-long backlog cannot adopt inline", r.adopted);
        assertNotNull("save must hand off to the worker", r.job);
        // The app starts the worker at its save call site; do the same here.
        ConversionService.startJob(ctx(), r.job.jobId);

        // The encoder must be gone: a survivor would still be writing the very
        // part file the worker now owns.
        long untilGone = System.currentTimeMillis() + 3000;
        while (streamThreadAlive() && System.currentTimeMillis() < untilGone) {
            Thread.sleep(50);
        }
        assertFalse("encoder thread outlived the abandoned adoption",
                streamThreadAlive());
        assertTrue("abandoned part file must not survive",
                !part.exists() || part.length() == 0);

        // And the worker must still produce a valid take from that raw: the
        // output it writes onto the same part path must be intact.
        ConversionJob job = ConversionJobs.get(r.job.jobId);
        long untilDone = System.currentTimeMillis() + 180000;
        while (System.currentTimeMillis() < untilDone) {
            job = ConversionJobs.get(r.job.jobId);
            if (job == null) break;
            if (ConversionJob.DONE.equals(job.state)
                    || ConversionJob.FAILED.equals(job.state)) break;
            Thread.sleep(250);
        }
        if (job != null) {
            assertEquals("conversion must succeed, not corrupt: " + job.error,
                    ConversionJob.DONE, job.state);
        }
        Take made = null;
        for (Take t : TakesRepository.all()) {
            if ("Abandoned adopt".equalsIgnoreCase(t.title)) { made = t; break; }
        }
        assertNotNull("no take was produced from the abandoned encoder", made);
        assertTrue("produced take has no file", made.filePath != null);
        File out = new File(made.filePath);
        assertTrue("produced file is missing", out.exists());
        // A corrupted container is exactly what two writers on one path makes.
        FormatConverter.validateFinal(out, SaveFormat.M4A);
        TakesRepository.delete(made.id);
        // Do not leave an orphan for the next test's sweep to adopt.
        // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
        out.delete();
    }

    /**
     * Sweep ran on every service start command while assuming it only ever ran
     * at cold start, so it deleted the partial file a live capture was still
     * writing and re-armed jobs already tracked in memory.
     */
    @Test
    public void sweepKeepsLiveCaptureAndTrackedJob() throws Exception {
        File dir = RecordingEngine.takesDir(ctx());
        RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
        engine.abortAndDelete();

        // A partial output with no sidecar: exactly what a live capture owns.
        File live = new File(dir, "sweep-live.wav");
        File livePart = new File(dir, "sweep-live.wav.part");
        writeRaw(live, 48000);
        writeEmpty(livePart);
        // The live capture also drops a .pending marker beside its raw.
        File pending = new File(dir, "sweep-live.wav.pending");
        pending.createNewFile();

        // A tracked job: in memory, so sweep must hand back the same instance
        // instead of a re-read copy reset to QUEUED.
        File raw2 = new File(dir, "sweep-job.wav");
        writeRaw(raw2, 24000);
        ConversionJob job = ConversionJobs.enqueue(ctx(), raw2, "Sweep job",
                RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.M4A, 500);
        ConversionJob inMemBefore = ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId);
        assertNotNull(inMemBefore);
        String stateBefore = inMemBefore.state;

        try {
            List<ConversionJob> resume = ConversionJobs.sweep(ctx());
            assertTrue("live capture's part file was swept",
                    livePart.exists());
            assertTrue("job was lost by the sweep",
                    ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId) != null);
            assertSame("sweep replaced a tracked job with a re-read copy",
                    inMemBefore, ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId));
            assertEquals("a tracked job was re-armed by the sweep",
                    stateBefore, ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId).state);
            boolean found = false;
            for (ConversionJob j : resume) {
                if (j.jobId.equals(job.jobId)) found = true;
            }
            assertTrue("tracked job missing from the resume list", found);
        } finally {
            ConversionJobs.cancel(job.jobId, false);
            // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
            pending.delete();
            // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
            live.delete();
            // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
            livePart.delete();
            // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
            raw2.delete();
        }
    }

    /**
     * Starting the service again for a job that is already running used to
     * re-queue it: its id had been polled off the queue, so the "already
     * queued" check missed it, and the second run reported a false failure
     * because the raw was already gone.
     */
    @Test
    public void repeatedStartServiceRunsTheJobOnce() throws Exception {
        RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
        engine.abortAndDelete();
        File dir = RecordingEngine.takesDir(ctx());
        File raw = new File(dir, "dedupe.wav");
        writeRaw(raw, 96000);
        int before = TakesRepository.all().size();
        ConversionJob job = ConversionJobs.enqueue(ctx(), raw, "Dedupe",
                RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.M4A, 2000);
        try {
            // Same job delivered twice, as happens when a second save starts
            // the service while the first job is still converting.
            ConversionService.startJob(ctx(), job.jobId);
            ConversionService.startJob(ctx(), job.jobId);

            long until = System.currentTimeMillis() + 120000;
            ConversionJob cur;
            while (System.currentTimeMillis() < until) {
                cur = ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId);
                // A finished job is retired from ACTIVE, so "gone" means done.
                if (cur == null
                        || ConversionJob.DONE.equals(cur.state)
                        || ConversionJob.FAILED.equals(cur.state)) break;
                Thread.sleep(250);
            }
            cur = ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId);
            if (cur != null) {
                assertEquals("duplicate execution reported a false failure: "
                        + cur.error, ConversionJob.DONE, cur.state);
            }
            assertEquals("job produced more than one take",
                    before + 1, TakesRepository.all().size());
            Take made = TakesRepository.all().get(0);
            assertNotNull(made.filePath);
            FormatConverter.validateFinal(new File(made.filePath),
                    SaveFormat.M4A);
            assertFalse("a part file was left behind",
                    ConversionJob.partFor(raw).exists());
        } finally {
            ConversionJobs.cancel(job.jobId, false);
            for (Take t : new java.util.ArrayList<>(TakesRepository.all())) {
                if ("Dedupe".equals(t.title)) {
                    TakesRepository.delete(t.id);
                    if (t.filePath != null) new File(t.filePath).delete();
                }
            }
            // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
            raw.delete();
        }
    }

    /**
     * Renaming a take while it converts must be the name the finished take
     * ends up with. The conversion captures its title when it starts, so a
     * rename made mid-flight used to be dropped and the take snapped back to
     * the original name the moment the card turned into a real take.
     */
    @Test
    public void renameDuringConversionReachesTheFinishedTake() throws Exception {
        RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
        engine.abortAndDelete();
        File raw = new File(RecordingEngine.takesDir(ctx()), "renamed.wav");
        long frames = 48000L * 90L;
        writeRaw(raw, (int) frames);
        int before = TakesRepository.all().size();

        ConversionJob job = ConversionJobs.enqueue(ctx(), raw,
                "Original name", RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.M4A, 90000);
        ConversionService.startJob(ctx(), job.jobId);
        try {
            // Wait until the worker is genuinely mid-conversion.
            ConversionJob cur = ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId);
            long until = System.currentTimeMillis() + 60000;
            while (System.currentTimeMillis() < until) {
                cur = ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId);
                if (cur == null) break;
                if (ConversionJob.RUNNING.equals(cur.state)) break;
                Thread.sleep(50);
            }
            assertNotNull("job never started", cur);
            assertEquals("conversion finished before it could be renamed; "
                    + "use a longer take", ConversionJob.RUNNING, cur.state);

            // This is what the library does when a converting card is renamed.
            assertEquals("rename helper rejected the new title",
                    "Renamed mid flight",
                    ConversionJobs.renameConvertingOrCompleted(
                            cur.jobId, cur.takeId(), cur.rawPath,
                            "Renamed mid flight"));

            until = System.currentTimeMillis() + 180000;
            while (System.currentTimeMillis() < until) {
                cur = ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId);
                if (cur == null) break;
                if (ConversionJob.DONE.equals(cur.state)
                        || ConversionJob.FAILED.equals(cur.state)) break;
                Thread.sleep(200);
            }
            if (cur != null) {
                assertEquals("conversion failed: " + cur.error,
                        ConversionJob.DONE, cur.state);
            }
            assertEquals("job produced more than one take",
                    before + 1, TakesRepository.all().size());
            Take made = TakesRepository.all().get(0);
            assertEquals("rename during conversion was dropped",
                    "Renamed mid flight", made.title);
            File out = new File(made.filePath);
            TakesRepository.delete(made.id);
            // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
            out.delete();
        } finally {
            ConversionJobs.cancel(job.jobId, false);
            // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
            raw.delete();
        }
    }

    private void writeRaw(File f, int frames) throws Exception {
        try (RandomAccessFile w = new RandomAccessFile(f, "rw")) {
            w.setLength(0);
            w.write(Dsp.wavFloatHeader(2, RecordingEngine.SAMPLE_RATE,
                    frames * 4L * 2));
            byte[] chunk = new byte[65536];
            long rem = (long) frames * 4L * 2L;
            while (rem > 0) {
                int n = (int) Math.min(chunk.length, rem);
                w.write(chunk, 0, n);
                rem -= n;
            }
        }
    }

    private void writeEmpty(File f) throws Exception {
        try (RandomAccessFile w = new RandomAccessFile(f, "rw")) {
            w.setLength(0);
        }
    }
}

package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertNotNull;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertNull;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import android.content.Context;

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4;
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry;

import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;

import java.io.File;
import java.io.RandomAccessFile;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Proves the background conversion path end to end: enqueue a job for a
 * synthetic raw take, run it through {@link ConversionService}, and assert
 * the finished take lands in the library while the raw is deleted.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class ConversionWorkerTest {

    private File makeRaw(Context ctx, String name) throws Exception {
        File takes = RecordingEngine.takesDir(ctx);
        File f = new File(takes, name + "_" + System.nanoTime() + ".wav");
        int frames = 48000 * 2; // 2s stereo
        RandomAccessFile w = new RandomAccessFile(f, "rw");
        try {
            w.setLength(0);
            w.write(Dsp.wavFloatHeader(2, 48000, (long) frames * 2 * 4));
            float[] buf = new float[frames * 2];
            for (int i = 0; i < frames * 2; i++) {
                buf[i] = (float) Math.sin(i * 0.05) * 0.4f;
            }
            Dsp.writeFloatsLE(w, buf, 0, buf.length);
        } finally {
            w.close();
        }
        return f;
    }

    @Test
    public void backgroundJobConvertsAndCleansUp() throws Exception {
        // Foreground activity so the conversion service may start.
        android.app.Instrumentation instr =
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation();
        android.content.Intent i = new android.content.Intent(
                instr.getTargetContext(), MainActivity.class);
        i.addFlags(android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK
                | android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK);
        instr.startActivitySync(i);
        Context ctx = instr.getTargetContext();
        File raw = makeRaw(ctx, "Worker");
        ConversionJob job = null;
        Take finished = null;
        try {
            job = ConversionJobs.enqueue(ctx, raw, "Worker Take",
                    RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.M4A, 2000);
            assertNotNull("no job", job);
            assertTrue("sidecar missing", job.sidecar().exists());
            ConversionService.startJob(ctx, job.jobId);

            long t0 = System.currentTimeMillis();
            while (ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId) != null
                    && System.currentTimeMillis() - t0 < 60_000) {
                Thread.sleep(500);
            }
            assertNull("job never finished",
                    ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId));

            List<Take> takes = TakesRepository.all();
            for (Take t : takes) {
                if ("Worker Take".equals(t.title)) finished = t;
            }
            assertNotNull("finished take not in library", finished);
            assertTrue("finished file missing",
                    finished.hasFile());
            assertTrue("raw was not deleted", !raw.exists());
            assertTrue("sidecar was not deleted", !job.sidecar().exists());
        } finally {
            if (finished != null) {
                TakesRepository.delete(finished.id);
                File f = new File(finished.filePath);
                if (f.exists()) {
                    // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
                    f.delete();
                }
            }
            if (job != null) ConversionJobs.cancel(job.jobId, true);
            if (raw.exists()) {
                // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
                raw.delete();
            }
        }
    }
}

package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertNotNull;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertNull;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import android.content.Context;

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4;
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry;

import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;

import java.io.File;
import java.io.RandomAccessFile;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * BUG-02 on device: an edit punch-in saved through the background worker
 * honours the replace choice — the original take is replaced under its own
 * title instead of duplicating the library.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class EditReplaceWorkerTest {

    private File makeRaw(Context ctx, String name) throws Exception {
        File takes = RecordingEngine.takesDir(ctx);
        File f = new File(takes, name + "_" + System.nanoTime() + ".wav");
        int frames = 48000 * 2; // 2s stereo
        RandomAccessFile w = new RandomAccessFile(f, "rw");
        try {
            w.setLength(0);
            w.write(Dsp.wavFloatHeader(2, 48000, (long) frames * 2 * 4));
            float[] buf = new float[frames * 2];
            for (int i = 0; i < frames * 2; i++) {
                buf[i] = (float) Math.sin(i * 0.05) * 0.4f;
            }
            Dsp.writeFloatsLE(w, buf, 0, buf.length);
        } finally {
            w.close();
        }
        return f;
    }

    private void runToDone(ConversionJob job) throws Exception {
        ConversionService.startJob(
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().getTargetContext(),
                job.jobId);
        long t0 = System.currentTimeMillis();
        while (ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId) != null
                && System.currentTimeMillis() - t0 < 60_000) {
            Thread.sleep(500);
        }
        assertNull("job never finished", ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId));
    }

    private Take findByTitle(String title) {
        for (Take t : TakesRepository.all()) {
            if (title.equals(t.title)) return t;
        }
        return null;
    }

    @Test
    public void backgroundSaveWithReplaceLineageReplacesOriginal()
            throws Exception {
        android.app.Instrumentation instr =
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation();
        android.content.Intent i = new android.content.Intent(
                instr.getTargetContext(), MainActivity.class);
        i.addFlags(android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK
                | android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK);
        instr.startActivitySync(i);
        Context ctx = instr.getTargetContext();

        // 1) A finished "original" take in the library.
        File raw1 = makeRaw(ctx, "EditOrig");
        ConversionJob j1 = ConversionJobs.enqueue(ctx, raw1, "Edit Original",
                RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.M4A, 2000);
        runToDone(j1);
        Take original = findByTitle("Edit Original");
        assertNotNull("original take missing", original);
        String originalPath = original.filePath;

        // 2) An edit of it, saved to the background worker with replace.
        File raw2 = makeRaw(ctx, "EditNew");
        ConversionJob j2 = ConversionJobs.enqueue(ctx, raw2, "Edit Session",
                RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.M4A, 2000,
                original.id, original.title);
        Take replaced = null;
        try {
            runToDone(j2);
            replaced = findByTitle("Edit Original");
            assertNotNull("replacement take missing", replaced);
            assertTrue("replacement must preserve immutable recording ID",
                    replaced.id == original.id);
            assertTrue("replacement has no file", replaced.hasFile());
        } finally {
            if (replaced != null) {
                TakesRepository.delete(replaced.id);
                File f = new File(replaced.filePath);
                if (f.exists()) f.delete();
            } else {
                Take leftover = findByTitle("Edit Session");
                if (leftover != null) TakesRepository.delete(leftover.id);
            }
            Take orig = findByTitle("Edit Original");
            if (orig != null && (replaced == null
                    || orig.id != replaced.id)) {
                TakesRepository.delete(orig.id);
            }
            ConversionJobs.cancel(j2.jobId, true);
            if (raw2.exists()) raw2.delete();
        }
    }
}

package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertArrayEquals;

/**
 * Runs the real encode/mux path on a real device image, one format per test
 * method. Robolectric stubs MediaCodec out, so this is the only way to see
 * which container actually works on a given Android build.
 *
 * <p>Each method is independent on purpose: a native crash in one encoder
 * kills the process and would hide the results of the rest.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class EncodeFormatsTest {

    private static final String TAG = "ENCFMT";

    private File makeFloatWav(String name) throws Exception {
        Context ctx = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
                .getTargetContext();
        File f = new File(ctx.getCacheDir(), name);
        int frames = 48000; // 1.0s at 48 kHz, stereo
        byte[] hdr = Dsp.wavFloatHeader(2, 48000, (long) frames * 2 * 4);
        RandomAccessFile w = new RandomAccessFile(f, "rw");
        try {
            w.setLength(0);
            w.write(hdr);
            float[] buf03 = new float[frames * 2];
            for (int i = 0; i < frames * 2; i++) {
                buf03[i] = (float) Math.sin(i * 0.03) * 0.5f;
            }
            Dsp.writeFloatsLE(w, buf03, 0, buf03.length);
        } finally {
            w.close();
        }
        return f;
    }

    private File out(String ext) {
        Context ctx = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
                .getTargetContext();
        File f = new File(ctx.getCacheDir(), "out_" + System.nanoTime() + ext);
        // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
        f.delete();
        return f;
    }

    @Test
    public void wav16() throws Exception {
        File src = makeFloatWav("wav16_in.wav");
        File dst = out(".wav");
        FormatConverter.toWav16(src, dst, null);
        Log.i(TAG, "PASS wav16 bytes=" + dst.length());
        assertTrue(dst.length() > 1000);
    }

    @Test
    public void m4a() throws Exception {
        File src = makeFloatWav("m4a_in.wav");
        File dst = out(".m4a");
        FormatConverter.toM4a(src, dst, 128000, null);
        Log.i(TAG, "PASS m4a bytes=" + dst.length());
        FormatConverter.validateFinal(dst, SaveFormat.M4A);
        assertTrue(dst.length() > 512);
    }

    @Test
    public void opus() throws Exception {
        File src = makeFloatWav("opus_in.wav");
        File dst = out("." + SaveFormat.OPUS.extension());
        FormatConverter.toOpus(src, dst, 128000, null);
        Log.i(TAG, "PASS opus bytes=" + dst.length());
        FormatConverter.validateFinal(dst, SaveFormat.OPUS);
        assertTrue(dst.length() > 512);
    }

    @Test
    public void flac() throws Exception {
        File src = makeFloatWav("flac_in.wav");
        File dst = out(".flac");
        FormatConverter.toFlac(src, dst, null);
        Log.i(TAG, "PASS flac bytes=" + dst.length());
        FormatConverter.validateFinal(dst, SaveFormat.FLAC);
        assertTrue(dst.length() > 512);
    }

    @Test
    public void amrNb() throws Exception {
        File src = makeFloatWav("amrnb_in.wav");
        File dst = out(".3gp");
        FormatConverter.toAmr(src, dst, false, null);
        Log.i(TAG, "PASS amrnb bytes=" + dst.length());
        assertTrue(dst.length() > 512);
    }

    @Test

        File src = makeFloatWav("amrwb_in.wav");
        File dst = out(".3gp");
        FormatConverter.toAmr(src, dst, true, null);
        Log.i(TAG, "PASS amrwb bytes=" + dst.length());
        assertTrue(dst.length() > 512);

    /** The full save pipeline, exactly as the save button drives it. */
    @Test
    public void fullSavePipeline() throws Exception {
        Context ctx = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
                .getTargetContext();
        RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
        engine.clearSession();
        engine.startNewSession(ctx, "Instrumentation", 2);
        File raw = engine.rawFile;
        assertNotNull(raw);
        int frames = 24000;
        RandomAccessFile w = new RandomAccessFile(raw, "rw");
        try {
            w.seek(w.length());
            float[] buf05 = new float[frames * 2];
            for (int i = 0; i < frames * 2; i++) {
                buf05[i] = (float) Math.sin(i * 0.05) * 0.4f;
            }
            Dsp.writeFloatsLE(w, buf05, 0, buf05.length);
        } finally {
            w.close();
        }
        TakeSaver.Result r = TakeSaver.finalizeAndConvert(ctx,
                RecordPreset.MUSIC, SaveFormat.WAV16, null);
        Log.i(TAG, "PASS pipeline file=" + r.file.getName()
                + " bytes=" + r.file.length() + " dur=" + r.durationMs);
        try {
            assertTrue(r.file.exists());
        } finally {
            engine.clearSession();
            r.file.delete();
        }
    }

    /** Real 24-bit encode: our own pure-Java path, fully testable on device. */
    @Test
    public void wav24Encode() throws Exception {
        File src = makeFloatWav("wav24_in.wav");
        File dst = out(".wav");
        FormatConverter.toWav24(src, dst, null);
        Log.i(TAG, "PASS wav24 bytes=" + dst.length());
        assertTrue(dst.length() > 1000);
        // 24-bit stereo 48k must be exactly 3/4 of the 32-bit float input.
        long expect = (src.length() - 44) * 3 / 4;
        assertEquals("unexpected 24-bit payload size", expect + 44,
                dst.length());
        FormatConverter.validateFinal(dst, SaveFormat.WAV24);
        // Duration must survive the 3-byte sample assembly.
        long dur = Dsp.wavDurationMs(dst);
        Log.i(TAG, "PASS wav24 duration=" + dur);
        assertTrue("duration off: " + dur, dur >= 950 && dur <= 1050);
    }

    /** WAV32 is the raw capture: header plus a byte-exact float payload. */
    @Test
    public void wav32Encode() throws Exception {
        File src = makeFloatWav("wav32_in.wav");
        File dst = out(".wav");
        FormatConverter.toWav32(src, dst, null);
        Log.i(TAG, "PASS wav32 bytes=" + dst.length());
        assertEquals(src.length(), dst.length());
        FormatConverter.validateFinal(dst, SaveFormat.WAV32);
        assertArrayEquals(readAll(src), readAll(dst));
        long dur = Dsp.wavDurationMs(dst);
        Log.i(TAG, "PASS wav32 duration=" + dur);
        assertTrue("duration off: " + dur, dur >= 950 && dur <= 1050);
    }

    private static byte[] readAll(File f) throws Exception {
        java.io.RandomAccessFile r = new java.io.RandomAccessFile(f, "r");
        try {
            byte[] out = new byte[(int) r.length()];
            r.readFully(out);
            return out;
        } finally {
            r.close();
        }
    }

    /** Music + Auto must stay lossless (WAV32) and must never land on a lossy codec. */
    @Test
    public void musicAutoStaysLossless() throws Exception {
        Context ctx = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
                .getTargetContext();
        RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
        engine.clearSession();
        engine.startNewSession(ctx, "Music Auto", 2);
        File raw = engine.rawFile;
        int frames = 24000;
        RandomAccessFile w = new RandomAccessFile(raw, "rw");
        try {
            w.seek(w.length());
            float[] buf05 = new float[frames * 2];
            for (int i = 0; i < frames * 2; i++) {
                buf05[i] = (float) Math.sin(i * 0.05) * 0.4f;
            }
            Dsp.writeFloatsLE(w, buf05, 0, buf05.length);
        } finally {
            w.close();
        }
        TakeSaver.Result r = TakeSaver.finalizeAndConvert(ctx,
                RecordPreset.MUSIC, SaveFormat.AUTO, null);
        Log.i(TAG, "LOSSLESS label=" + r.label + " bytes=" + r.file.length());
        try {
            assertEquals("music auto must be WAV32: " + r.label,
                    "WAV32", r.label);
            assertTrue(r.file.exists());
            FormatConverter.validateFinal(r.file, SaveFormat.WAV32);
            assertFalse("raw must be cleaned up", raw.exists());
        } finally {
            engine.clearSession();
            r.file.delete();
        }
    }
}

package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertNotNull;

import android.content.Context;

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4;
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry;

import org.json.JSONArray;
import org.json.JSONObject;
import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;

import java.io.File;
import java.io.FileInputStream;
import java.io.FileOutputStream;
import java.io.InputStream;
import java.io.OutputStreamWriter;
import java.io.Writer;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;

/**
 * Tier 3 of the FX verification harness: converts the uploaded 32-bit float WAV
 * into every container the app can write and records exactly what came out, so
 * the container/codec claims can be checked independently (with ffprobe) rather
 * than trusted.
 *
 * <p>Formats that need a hardware/software encoder are probed first, and a
 * format the device cannot encode is reported as skipped with its reason.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class FormatMatrixDeviceTest {

    @Test
    public void convertTheUploadedClipIntoEveryFormat() throws Exception {
        Context ctx = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().getTargetContext();
        File work = new File(RecordingEngine.takesDir(ctx), "fxverify-formats");
        work.mkdirs();

        File input = new File(work, "input.wav");
        copyAsset("take2_48k_f32.wav", input);
        FxVerifySupportDevice.WavInfo info = FxVerifySupportDevice.readInfo(input);

        JSONObject root = new JSONObject();
        root.put("input", "input.wav");
        root.put("inputFrames", info.frames);
        root.put("inputChannels", info.channels);
        root.put("inputSampleRate", info.sampleRate);
        root.put("inputAudioFormat", info.audioFormat);
        root.put("inputBits", info.bits);
        JSONArray results = new JSONArray();

        for (SaveFormat fmt : SaveFormat.values()) {
            JSONObject entry = new JSONObject();
            entry.put("id", fmt.id);
            entry.put("extension", fmt.extension());
            entry.put("effective", fmt.effective(RecordPreset.PODCAST).id);
            try {
                if (!fmt.available(ctx)) {
                    entry.put("skipped", "no encoder for " + fmt.encoderMime());
                    results.put(entry);
                    continue;
                }
                SaveFormat effective = fmt.effective(RecordPreset.PODCAST);
                TakeSaver.Result r = TakeSaver.convertRaw(ctx, input,
                        "take2-" + fmt.id, RecordPreset.PODCAST, fmt, null);
                assertNotNull("convertRaw returned nothing for " + fmt.id, r);
                assertNotNull("no file for " + fmt.id, r.file);
                File out = new File(work, "fmt-" + fmt.id + "." + r.file.getName()
                        .substring(r.file.getName().lastIndexOf('.') + 1));
                copy(r.file, out);
                entry.put("file", out.getName());
                entry.put("bytes", out.length());
                entry.put("label", r.label);
                entry.put("durationMs", r.durationMs);
                entry.put("title", r.title);
                entry.put("effectiveId", effective.id);
                try {
                    FormatConverter.validateFinal(out, effective);
                    entry.put("validateFinal", "ok");
                } catch (Throwable t) {
                    entry.put("validateFinal", "failed: " + t.getMessage());
                }
                entry.put("probe", probeHeader(out));
            } catch (Throwable t) {
                entry.put("error", t.getClass().getSimpleName() + ": " + t.getMessage());
            }
            results.put(entry);
        }

        JSONArray strays = new JSONArray();
        File[] siblings = work.getParentFile() == null ? new File[0]
                : work.getParentFile().listFiles();
        if (siblings != null) {
            for (File f : siblings) {
                if (f.getName().endsWith(".part") || f.getName().contains(".png")) {
                    strays.put(f.getName());
                }
            }
        }
        root.put("leftoverParts", strays);
        root.put("results", results);

        try (Writer w = new OutputStreamWriter(
                new FileOutputStream(new File(work, "formats.json")),
                StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
            w.write(root.toString(2));
        }
        System.out.println("Format matrix: " + results.length() + " formats attempted");
    }

    /** First bytes of the container, so the analysis side can check the magic. */
    private static String probeHeader(File f) throws Exception {
        try (InputStream in = new FileInputStream(f)) {
            byte[] head = new byte[16];
            int n = in.read(head);
            StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
            for (int i = 0; i < Math.max(0, n); i++) {
                sb.append(String.format("%02x", head[i]));
            }
            return sb.toString();
        }
    }

    private static void copyAsset(String name, File dest) throws Exception {
        try (InputStream in = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
                .getContext().getAssets().open(name);
             FileOutputStream out = new FileOutputStream(dest)) {
            byte[] buf = new byte[65536];
            int n;
            while ((n = in.read(buf)) > 0) out.write(buf, 0, n);
        }
    }

    private static void copy(File src, File dst) throws Exception {
        try (InputStream in = new FileInputStream(src);
             FileOutputStream out = new FileOutputStream(dst)) {
            byte[] buf = new byte[65536];
            int n;
            while ((n = in.read(buf)) > 0) out.write(buf, 0, n);
        }
    }
}

FILE: app/src/androidTest/java/com/example/hello/FormatRoundTripTest.java

package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertNotNull;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import android.content.Context;
import android.media.MediaPlayer;

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4;
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry;

import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;

import java.io.File;
import java.io.RandomAccessFile;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Format round trip on a real decoder (FMT-01/FMT-02/FMT-03).
 *
 * <p>For every save format: encode a known tone, pass the strict container
 * validation, prove the platform can actually open it (MediaPlayer.prepare),
 * and prove the Edit path can decode it back to a 48 kHz float session at the
 * right pitch. This is the test that catches a malformed FLAC header, which
 * previously produced files Android silently refused to play or edit.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class FormatRoundTripTest {

    private File makeTone(Context ctx, String name, int frames, int ch)
            throws Exception {
        File f = new File(ctx.getCacheDir(), name);
        RandomAccessFile w = new RandomAccessFile(f, "rw");
        try {
            w.setLength(0);
            w.write(Dsp.wavFloatHeader(ch, 48000, (long) frames * ch * 4));
            float[] buf = new float[frames * ch];
            for (int i = 0; i < frames; i++) {
                float v = (float) (0.4 * Math.sin(i * 0.05));
                for (int c = 0; c < ch; c++) buf[i * ch + c] = v;
            }
            Dsp.writeFloatsLE(w, buf, 0, buf.length);
        } finally {
            w.close();
        }
        return f;
    }

    private static boolean canEncode(String id) {
        return SaveFormat.of(id).available(
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().getTargetContext());
    }

    @Test
    public void everyFormatValidatesPlaysAndImports() throws Exception {
        Context ctx = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
                .getTargetContext();
        String[] ids = {"wav16", "wav24", "m4a", "flac", "opus", "amr_nb",
                "amr_wb"};
        List<String> problems = new ArrayList<>();
        for (String id : ids) {
            SaveFormat fmt = SaveFormat.of(id);
            if (!canEncode(id)) continue; // probe-gated on this device
            File raw = makeTone(ctx, "rt_" + id, 96000, 2); // 2.0 s
            File out = null;
            File back = null;
            try {
                TakeSaver.Result r = TakeSaver.convertRaw(ctx, raw,
                        "RoundTrip " + id, RecordPreset.PODCAST, fmt, null);
                out = r.file;
                assertNotNull("no output for " + id, out);
                // Strict container validation.
                FormatConverter.validateFinal(out, fmt);

                // Real decode through the platform.
                MediaPlayer mp = new MediaPlayer();
                try {
                    mp.setDataSource(out.getAbsolutePath());
                    mp.prepare();
                    int dur = mp.getDuration();
                    if (dur < 1200 || dur > 3200) {
                        problems.add(id + " duration " + dur + "ms");
                    }
                } catch (Exception e) {
                    problems.add(id + " not playable: " + e);
                } finally {
                    try {
                        mp.release();
                    } catch (Exception ignored) {}
                }

                // Edit path: decode back to a 48 kHz float session.
                back = AudioImporter.takeToFloatWav(out,
                        RecordingEngine.takesDir(ctx), "RT " + id, null);
                FormatConverter.WavInfo info =
                        FormatConverter.readFloatWav(back);
                if (info.sampleRate != 48000) {
                    problems.add(id + " import rate " + info.sampleRate);
                }
                if (info.dataBytes <= 0) problems.add(id + " empty import");
                double pitch = pitchHz(back);
                // ~382 Hz tone; allow for lossy codecs and resampling.
                if (pitch < 330 || pitch > 440) {
                    problems.add(id + " pitch " + Math.round(pitch) + "Hz");
                }
                float peak = peakAbs(back);
                if (peak < 0.15f || peak > 0.8f) {
                    problems.add(id + " peak " + peak);
                }
            } catch (Exception e) {
                problems.add(id + " threw " + e);
            } finally {
                if (out != null) {
                    // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
                    out.delete();
                }
                if (back != null) {
                    // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
                    back.delete();
                }
                if (raw.exists()) {
                    // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
                    raw.delete();
                }
            }
        }
        assertTrue("round-trip problems: " + problems, problems.isEmpty());
    }

    private static float peakAbs(File wav) throws Exception {
        FormatConverter.WavInfo info = FormatConverter.readFloatWav(wav);
        RandomAccessFile r = new RandomAccessFile(wav, "r");
        try {
            int ch = info.channels;
            long frames = info.dataBytes / 4 / ch;
            int n = (int) Math.min(frames, 48000);
            byte[] raw = new byte[n * ch * 4];
            r.seek(info.dataStart);
            r.readFully(raw);
            java.nio.FloatBuffer fb = java.nio.ByteBuffer.wrap(raw)
                    .order(java.nio.ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN).asFloatBuffer();
            float peak = 0f;
            for (int i = 0; i < n * ch; i++) {
                peak = Math.max(peak, Math.abs(fb.get(i)));
            }
            return peak;
        } finally {
            r.close();
        }
    }

    private static double pitchHz(File wav) throws Exception {
        FormatConverter.WavInfo info = FormatConverter.readFloatWav(wav);
        RandomAccessFile r = new RandomAccessFile(wav, "r");
        try {
            int ch = info.channels;
            long frames = info.dataBytes / 4 / ch;
            int n = (int) Math.min(frames, 48000);
            byte[] raw = new byte[n * ch * 4];
            r.seek(info.dataStart);
            r.readFully(raw);
            java.nio.FloatBuffer fb = java.nio.ByteBuffer.wrap(raw)
                    .order(java.nio.ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN).asFloatBuffer();
            int crossings = 0;
            float prev = fb.get(0);
            for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {
                float cur = fb.get(i * ch);
                if ((prev <= 0f && cur > 0f) || (prev >= 0f && cur < 0f)) {
                    crossings++;
                }
                prev = cur;
            }
            return crossings / 2.0 / (n / (double) info.sampleRate);
        } finally {
            r.close();
        }
    }
}

FILE: app/src/androidTest/java/com/example/hello/FormatSpeedAuditTest.java
=================================================================================
package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import android.content.Context;
import android.media.MediaPlayer;

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4;
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry;

import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;

import java.io.File;
import java.io.RandomAccessFile;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * Audits why AMR converts so much faster than the other formats, and proves
 * the speed is real work done cheaply rather than skipped work.
 *
 * <p>AMR is the odd one out for three compounding reasons:
 * <ul>
 *   <li>It is the only format that decimates before encoding: 48 kHz to 8 kHz
 *       (AMR-NB) or 16 kHz (AMR-WB), so one sixth or one third of the samples
 *       ever reach the encoder.</li>
 *   <li>It encodes at 12.2 kbps / 23.85 kbps, against 128 kbps for M4A and
 *       far more for lossless, so the muxer handles a fraction of the data.</li>
 *   <li>Every sample it does handle is mono, half the channels of the
 *       source.</li>
 * </ul>
 *
 * <p>The bug this test exists to catch is the opposite one: an encoder that
 * returns quickly because it truncated or skipped frames. The take duration
 * shown in the library comes from the raw file, not the output, so a truncated
 * AMR would still look correct in the UI. These assertions therefore measure
 * the encoded file itself: decoded duration must match the source, and the
 * byte count must match the declared bitrate over that duration.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class FormatSpeedAuditTest {

    private static final String TAG = "FormatSpeed";
    private static final int SECONDS = 10;
    private static final int RATE = 48000;

    private File makeTone(Context ctx, String name, int seconds, int ch)
            throws Exception {
        File raw = new File(RecordingEngine.takesDir(ctx), name + ".wav");
        long frames = (long) RATE * seconds;
        byte[] chunk = new byte[16384 * ch * 4];
        try (RandomAccessFile w = new RandomAccessFile(raw, "rw")) {
            w.setLength(0);
            w.write(Dsp.wavFloatHeader(ch, RATE, frames * 4L * ch));
            long written = 0;
            while (written < frames) {
                int want = (int) Math.min(16384, frames - written);
                java.nio.ByteBuffer bb =
                        java.nio.ByteBuffer.wrap(chunk).order(
                                java.nio.ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN);
                bb.clear();
                for (int i = 0; i < want; i++) {
                    double t = (written + i) / (double) RATE;
                    float v = (float) (0.4 * Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * 440 * t));
                    for (int c = 0; c < ch; c++) bb.putFloat(v);
                }
                w.write(chunk, 0, want * ch * 4);
                written += want;
            }
        }
        return raw;
    }

    private boolean canEncode(String id) {
        try {
            return SaveFormat.of(id).available(
                    InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
                            .getTargetContext());
        } catch (Throwable t) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    private int decodedDurationMs(File f) {
        MediaPlayer mp = new MediaPlayer();
        try {
            mp.setDataSource(f.getAbsolutePath());
            mp.prepare();
            return mp.getDuration();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return -1;
        } finally {
            try {
                mp.release();
            } catch (Exception ignored) {}
        }
    }

    /** Nominal bytes for the format's declared bitrate over SECONDS. */
    private long nominalBytes(SaveFormat fmt) {
        int bitrate;
        switch (fmt) {
            case AMR_NB: bitrate = 12200; break;
            case AMR_WB: bitrate = 23850; break;
            case M4A: bitrate = 128000; break;
            case OPUS: bitrate = 96000; break;
            case FLAC: return -1; // lossless, no fixed bitrate
            default: return -1;
        }
        return bitrate * SECONDS / 8L;
    }

    @Test
    public void amrIsFastBecauseItEncodesFarLessDataAndKeepsFullDuration()
            throws Exception {
        Context ctx = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
                .getTargetContext();
        File raw = makeTone(ctx, "speed", SECONDS, 2);
        String[] ids = {"wav16", "m4a", "flac", "opus", "amr_nb", "amr_wb"};

        Map<String, String> table = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        Map<String, Long> ms = new LinkedHashMap<>();

        try {
            for (String id : ids) {
                SaveFormat fmt = SaveFormat.of(id);
                if (!canEncode(id)) {
                    android.util.Log.i(TAG, id + ": unavailable here");
                    continue;
                }
                File out = null;
                try {
                    long t0 = System.nanoTime();
                    TakeSaver.Result r = TakeSaver.convertRaw(ctx, raw,
                            "Speed " + id, RecordPreset.MEMO, fmt, null);
                    long took = (System.nanoTime() - t0) / 1_000_000L;
                    out = r.file;
                    assertTrue("no output for " + id,
                            out != null && out.exists());
                    FormatConverter.validateFinal(out, fmt);

                    int dur = decodedDurationMs(out);
                    // The whole take must be there. A truncated or skipped
                    // encode shows up here, not in the library duration.
                    assertTrue(id + " decoded duration " + dur + "ms, expected "
                            + (SECONDS * 1000 - 600) + ".."
                            + (SECONDS * 1000 + 900),
                            dur > SECONDS * 1000 - 600
                                    && dur < SECONDS * 1000 + 900);

                    long nominal = nominalBytes(fmt);
                    if (nominal > 0) {
                        // Within +-35% of bitrate * duration: the encoder
                        // really did write that much audio.
                        double ratio = out.length() / (double) nominal;
                        assertTrue(id + " wrote " + out.length() + " bytes, "
                                        + "nominal " + nominal + " (ratio "
                                        + Math.round(ratio * 100) + "%)",
                                ratio > 0.65 && ratio < 1.35);
                    }
                    ms.put(id, took);
                    table.put(id, took + "ms, " + out.length() + "B, "
                            + dur + "ms audio");
                } finally {
                    if (out != null) {
                        // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
                        out.delete();
                    }
                }
            }

            for (Map.Entry<String, String> e : table.entrySet()) {
                android.util.Log.i(TAG, e.getKey() + " -> " + e.getValue());
            }

            // The user's observation, made an assertion: AMR really is the
            // quick one, because it hands the codec 1/6 of the samples.
            Long amr = ms.get("amr_nb");
            Long lossless = ms.get("flac");
            Long aac = ms.get("m4a");
            assertTrue("AMR-NB did not finish: " + ms, amr != null);
            // Compared against real codecs only: WAV16/WAV24 are byte
            // conversions with no encoder, so they can legitimately beat any
            // codec and say nothing about encoding cost.
            if (lossless != null) {
                assertTrue("AMR-NB (" + amr + "ms) should beat FLAC ("
                        + lossless + "ms)", amr < lossless);
            }
            if (aac != null) {
                assertTrue("AMR-NB (" + amr + "ms) should beat M4A/AAC ("
                        + aac + "ms)", amr < aac);
            }

            // And the decoded audio is real, not a valid-length empty file:
            // import it back and confirm the tone survived.
            File amrOut = TakeSaver.convertRaw(ctx, raw, "Speed amr back",
                    RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.AMR_NB, null).file;
            File back = null;
            try {
                back = AudioImporter.takeToFloatWav(amrOut,
                        RecordingEngine.takesDir(ctx), "Speed back", null);
                FormatConverter.WavInfo info =
                        FormatConverter.readFloatWav(back);
                assertEquals("imported rate", RATE, info.sampleRate);
                float peak = 0f;
                long n = info.dataBytes / 4L;
                try (RandomAccessFile r = new RandomAccessFile(back, "r")) {
                    r.seek(info.dataStart);
                    byte[] b = new byte[(int) Math.min(info.dataBytes,
                            65536L)];
                    r.readFully(b);
                    java.nio.ByteBuffer bb = java.nio.ByteBuffer.wrap(b)
                            .order(java.nio.ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN);
                    while (bb.remaining() >= 4) {
                        peak = Math.max(peak, Math.abs(bb.getFloat()));
                    }
                }
                assertTrue("AMR import is silent (peak " + peak + ", frames "
                        + n + ")", peak > 0.05f);
            } finally {
                if (back != null) back.delete();
                // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
                amrOut.delete();
            }
        } finally {
            // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
            raw.delete();
        }
    }
}
